doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: John Lewis, Ram Ramirez, and Bud Powell at Minton's jam sessions
summary: First gigs around New York, Tony Scott collecting him, and being bumped off the bandstand by Bud Powell at Minton's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: She just understood intuitively that she just was that broadminded. And I’m sure a lot of jazz people got in that way. So it was a very lively time I had there, and I became friends with John and I started working gigs around town. My first close friend was, I lived over a little nightclub called the Little Casino and one of the five pianists there was Ram Ramirez, the guy that wrote “Lover Man.” Wonderful piano player. So I became friends with him and then I joined the union and I started playing jobs and somewhere along the line Tony Scott got in the act and he collected me. He was like this wild egomaniac gifted man. And we wound up at Minton’s and that was like a postgraduate degree.
Oh man. Monday nights was jam session night, and everybody would come in and I got bumped off the bandstand by the best, including Bud Powell.
How would that happen? Getting bumped off the bench?

How would that happen? You’re playing along and this guy’s standing over your shoulder says, “Get up.” And you look and you see it’s Bud Powell. And you’re not in a position to say sorry. I mean you could but you don’t. So he would sit down and play like 20 choruses of “Crazy Rhythm” without ever once playing the bridge. But it didn’t matter. I had some fantastic experiences up there.
